The idiom is tshad mar byed pa, 'to treat as valid/authoritative' (tshad ma 'valid' + terminative -r); tsha dmar parses as tsha ('hot/salt') + dmar ('red') and is meaningless in this frame. GMR's English in THIS segment is 'we must look on this Word of the Buddha as perfectly accurate' -- that is tshad mar byed and nothing else. The segment's OWN ACIP is keyed the same way, 'BKA' LA TSA DMAR BYED DE' (ACIP TSA = tsha; the correct form would be TSAD MAR), so the D is misplaced in the source keying and the defect is not an artefact of the EWTS converter. CORROBORATION (other segments, cited only for the correct spelling, not as the defect): 'tshad mar byed' occurs three times in the spine -- C05:78 'mdo tshad mar byed kyi mngon pa sde bdun', whose English renders it 'holds that sutra is valid'; ILL:3267 'lung tshad mar byed pa la'; and DDA:372 'de la yid ches tshad mar byed', which pairs the idiom with the very same yid ches this segment ends on. PARALLEL-WITNESS CHECK PERFORMED: 'tsha dmar' occurs exactly twice in the entire spine -- C03:420 and P1:72. P1:72 is this same Bodongwa passage ingested a second time (Wylie identical apart from punctuation; English identical apart from two defects of its own, 'we must to look' and 'fromold age'), so it is a duplicate of the same source, not an independent witness, and it does not establish tsha dmar as a published variant reading. No other spine text spells the collocation 'tsha dmar' anywhere. Filed as an upstream source-keying defect, not as an ingest corruption of C03:420.
